rules: The agent may edit ONLY the 'status' and 'completed_at' fields of a feature. Nothing else in this file may be changed.
Set status to 'done' only after the 'verify' check passes AND every 'acceptance' item is true. Then set completed_at (YYYY-MM-DD) and append an entry to progress.md.
Work on the first feature in array order whose status is 'todo' and whose depends_on features are all 'done'.
Never add, remove, reorder or reword features. If a feature is wrong or impossible, set it to 'blocked' and tell the user why.
Steps that start with 'USER:' must be done by the human. Stop and ask, do not fake them.

features.title: Development environment and Git repo
features.description: Working Python virtual environment, VS Code interpreter selected, Git repo initialised with a safe .gitignore.
steps: USER: confirm OS (Windows/Mac/Linux). Python 3.14 may lack prebuilt wheels for chromadb / torch / sentence-transformers. Recommend installing Python 3.12 and using it for the venv; if the user insists on 3.14, test 'pip install chromadb sentence-transformers' first and fall back to 3.12 if it fails.
Create the project folder 'recipegen-ai' and a virtual environment '.venv' with the chosen Python version.
Select the .venv interpreter in VS Code.
Run 'git init'. Create .gitignore covering .venv/, .env, __pycache__/, chroma_db/, *.sqlite3, data/raw/, .pytest_cache/.
Create the GitHub repo (empty) and connect it as 'origin'.
acceptance: Inside the venv, python --version shows the chosen version.
git status does not list .venv or .env.
Repo exists on GitHub and 'git remote -v' shows it.

features.title: Project structure and base dependencies
features.description: Create the folder layout from overview.md and install the Milestone 1 dependencies.
steps: Create folders: recipegen/, tests/, data/raw, data/processed, eval/, scripts/, docs/.
Create empty module files listed in overview.md (with __init__.py in recipegen/ and tests/).
Create requirements.txt with: streamlit, google-genai, python-dotenv, pydantic, pytest. Install them.
Create a minimal README.md with the project name and one-line description.
acceptance: Folder layout matches overview.md.
All base packages import without error.
features.verify: python -c "import streamlit, pydantic, dotenv; from google import genai; print('ok')"

features.title: Gemini API key and hello-world call
features.description: Get a Gemini key from Google AI Studio (not OpenAI; the project uses Gemini) and make one successful API call.
steps: USER: create a Gemini API key in Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com). Do not paste it into chat or commit it.
USER: put it in a local .env file as GEMINI_API_KEY=... ; also set GEMINI_MODEL (check Google's current model list; do not rely on model names from memory).
Create .env.example with placeholder values only (this one IS committed).
Create recipegen/config.py that loads settings from .env using python-dotenv and fails with a clear message if the key is missing.
Create scripts/hello_gemini.py that sends 'Say hello in one line' and prints the reply.
acceptance: hello_gemini.py prints a model reply.
.env is git-ignored and .env.example contains no real key.
Missing key gives a readable error, not a stack trace.

features.title: Input validation module
features.description: Pure-Python validation of user input before any API call.
steps: USER: confirm allowed ranges. Suggested defaults: ingredients 1-15 items, each 2-40 chars; cooking time 5-180 min; servings 1-10; total input under 500 chars.
Put limits as constants in config.py.
Create recipegen/validation.py with validate_inputs(...) returning a list of human-readable error strings (empty list = valid).
Handle: empty/whitespace ingredients, duplicates, non-numeric or negative time, servings out of range, over-long input.
Write tests/test_validation.py covering every rule, including boundary values.
acceptance: Each rule from Phase 3C has at least one passing and one failing test.
No Streamlit or API imports inside validation.py.

features.title: Structured request model
features.description: A pydantic RecipeRequest that normalises user input and carries the extra fields for the target audience.
steps: USER: confirm the extra fields beyond the document: spice_level (mild/medium/hot), equipment (e.g. single stove, pressure cooker, rice cooker, microwave), bachelor_mode (bool: few utensils, pantry staples, quick cleanup). Also confirm the cuisine list; suggested: South Indian, Tamil, Kerala, Andhra, Karnataka, Telangana, North Indian, Other.
Create recipegen/models.py with RecipeRequest: ingredients, cuisine, dietary_preference, max_cooking_time, servings, spice_level, equipment, bachelor_mode.
Normalise: lowercase, strip, de-duplicate ingredients.
USER: decide whether 'max cooking time' means cook time only or prep + cook. Record the answer as a comment in models.py and in docs/DECISIONS.md.
Write tests/test_models.py.
acceptance: The example request from Phase 3D (potato, onion, egg) builds and serializes to the documented JSON shape plus the new fields.
Decision on time semantics is written down.

features.title: Prompt builder
features.description: Turn a RecipeRequest into the prompt, following the template in the project document.
steps: Create recipegen/prompts.py with build_prompt(request) -> str and a SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION constant.
Include all fields, the 'identify additional ingredients' rule, and the rule: if constraints cannot be met, explain the limitation instead of inventing a solution.
Add bachelor_mode text: minimal utensils, common pantry ingredients, short cleanup.
Add a South Indian authenticity instruction only when cuisine is South Indian-type; do not claim authenticity the model cannot back.
Write tests/test_prompts.py asserting every request field appears in the prompt.
acceptance: Prompt for the Phase 3B example contains ingredients, cuisine, diet, time and servings.
Prompt asks for structured JSON output.

features.title: Gemini client wrapper with error handling
features.description: One function that sends a prompt to Gemini and handles timeouts, rate limits and bad responses.
steps: Create recipegen/llm_client.py using the official google-genai SDK; model from GEMINI_MODEL env var.
Define custom exceptions: LLMTimeoutError, LLMRateLimitError, LLMResponseError.
Retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on rate-limit / transient 5xx errors only.
Never log the API key or full prompts containing user data at INFO level.
Write tests/test_llm_client.py using a mocked client: success, 429, timeout, empty response.
acceptance: All four mocked scenarios behave as specified.
A real call through the wrapper succeeds.

features.title: Structured recipe schema and JSON output
features.description: Make Gemini return JSON that parses into a validated Recipe object.
steps: Add a Recipe model to models.py: name, servings, prep_time_min, cook_time_min, ingredients (name, quantity, unit, from_user flag), additional_ingredients, steps, notes, constraints_met, limitation_message.
Use Gemini structured output (JSON response mime type + schema) in llm_client.py; check current SDK docs for the exact parameter names.
On JSON parse or schema failure, do ONE repair retry, then raise LLMResponseError. Never treat invalid output as success.
Create tests/fixtures with a good JSON and several bad ones; write tests/test_recipe_parsing.py.
acceptance: Good fixture parses into Recipe; each bad fixture raises a clear error.
A live call returns a parsed Recipe for the Phase 3B example.

features.title: Response validation (fields, time, diet)
features.description: Check the generated recipe against the user's constraints before display.
steps: Create recipegen/response_validation.py returning a ValidationReport (passed, errors, warnings).
Field checks: non-empty name, at least one ingredient, usable steps, valid times and servings.
Time check against the semantics decided in F05. If exceeded: one regeneration with feedback, then show a visible warning. Never present estimates as guarantees.
USER: decide how to treat eggs for 'Vegetarian' (many tools offer a separate 'Eggetarian' option). Suggested dietary options: Vegetarian, Eggetarian, Non-Vegetarian, Vegan.
Diet keyword check using explicit keyword lists in a data file (meat, fish, egg, dairy, honey as relevant). Document that this is a first safeguard, not a guarantee.
Write tests/test_response_validation.py including: vegetarian request returning chicken fails; time over limit fails.
acceptance: Each check has passing and failing tests.
The diet decision is recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md.

features.title: Streamlit interface
features.description: The input form and display area, not yet wired to the AI.
steps: Create app.py with: ingredient input, cuisine select, dietary select, max time, servings, spice level, equipment, bachelor-mode toggle, Generate button, result area.
Show validation errors from validation.py inline; do not call the model when invalid.
Use st.session_state so results survive reruns.
Add a footer disclaimer: recipes, quantities, times and food-safety steps must be checked before use.
acceptance: streamlit run app.py opens in the browser.
Empty ingredients shows an error and nothing is generated.
features.verify: streamlit run app.py (manual: submit empty form, then a valid form)

features.title: End-to-end pipeline (Milestone 1 demo)
features.description: Connect UI -> validation -> prompt -> Gemini -> response validation -> display.
steps: Create recipegen/pipeline.py with generate_recipe(request, use_rag=False) that orchestrates the steps and returns recipe + ValidationReport.
Call it from app.py with st.spinner. Show friendly messages for each custom exception.
Render the recipe cleanly: name, times, ingredients table, numbered steps, warnings from validation.
Add a Regenerate button. Add a Save button that is visibly disabled until F26.
Write tests/test_pipeline.py with a mocked LLM client.
acceptance: The Phase 3B example produces a displayed recipe.
Forcing an API failure (bad key) shows a readable message.
Pipeline tests pass.
features.verify: pytest tests/test_pipeline.py -q ; streamlit run app.py (manual end-to-end)

features.title: Milestone 1 checkpoint: full tests, push, tag
features.description: Lock in Milestone 1 before starting RAG.
steps: Run the whole test suite and fix failures.
Update README with setup and run instructions.
Commit with clear messages, push to GitHub, tag v0.1-m1.
Append an interviewer-style critique of Milestone 1 weaknesses to progress.md.
acceptance: All tests pass.
Fresh clone + README instructions runs the app (agent describes the check; USER confirms).
Tag v0.1-m1 is on GitHub.

features.title: Choose and download the recipe dataset
features.description: Pick a dataset with a usable licence and enough South Indian coverage.
steps: Agent suggests candidates to search on Kaggle (for example Indian-food datasets with cuisine, ingredients, instructions and time fields). Agent must say it cannot verify current contents or licences.
USER: download the chosen file manually and place it in data/raw/ (agents cannot log in to Kaggle).
USER + agent: read the licence page. Record licence, source URL and download date in docs/DATA_LICENCE.md.
Record the column list and row count.
acceptance: Raw file exists in data/raw/ and is git-ignored.
docs/DATA_LICENCE.md states the licence and whether redistribution is allowed.
If the licence forbids use or redistribution, the feature is 'blocked' and a different dataset is chosen.

features.title: Inspect the raw data
features.description: Understand the data before cleaning it.
steps: Create scripts/inspect_data.py using Pandas.
Report: row count, columns and types, null counts per column, duplicate count, cuisine value counts, how many rows look South Indian, how many have time fields.
Write the findings to docs/data_report.md (generated by the script).
acceptance: docs/data_report.md exists with the numbers above.
The report states honestly if South Indian coverage is too thin to support the project focus.

features.title: Data cleaning script
features.description: Repeatable cleaning with Pandas. Raw data is never modified.
steps: Create scripts/clean_data.py. Read from data/raw/, write only to data/processed/.
Remove duplicates, strip HTML and stray formatting, normalise text, drop invalid or incomplete recipes.
Standardise ingredient names where reasonable (e.g. case, plurals). Do NOT invent missing quantities; keep unknowns as null.
Print how many rows each step removed.
Write tests/test_cleaning.py on a tiny hand-made DataFrame.
acceptance: Cleaning is idempotent: running twice gives the same output.
Tests pass and cover HTML stripping, duplicates and missing values.

features.title: Processed dataset in a consistent schema
features.description: Final structured recipe file used by retrieval.
steps: Define the schema: id, name, ingredients (list), instructions, cuisine, prep_time, cook_time, diet tag if the source provides one.
USER: decide whether to derive a veg/non-veg tag from ingredients when the source has none. Agent must not infer it silently.
Write data/processed/recipes.json (or CSV, agreed with the user).
Generate a short summary: final row count and South Indian subset size.
acceptance: Every row matches the schema.
Row count and subset size are recorded in progress.md.

features.title: Embeddings with Sentence Transformers
features.description: Convert recipe text into vectors.
steps: Add sentence-transformers and chromadb to requirements.txt and install (watch Python version issues from F01).
Create recipegen/embeddings.py with embed_texts(list[str]) using one fixed model name stored in config.py. Check the model name on the Sentence Transformers docs before choosing.
Decide the text to embed per recipe (name + ingredients + cuisine) and document why.
Sanity check: 'potato onion sandwich' is closer to a potato sandwich recipe than to an unrelated dessert.
acceptance: Embedding dimension is printed and recorded.
Sanity check passes on real rows from the processed data.

features.title: Store recipes in ChromaDB
features.description: Persistent vector collection with documents and metadata.
steps: Create scripts/build_index.py that embeds all processed recipes and upserts into a persistent ChromaDB collection in chroma_db/.
Store original text and metadata (cuisine, times, diet tag).
Make it idempotent (upsert by recipe id).
Print time taken and collection count.
acceptance: Collection count equals processed row count.
Re-running does not create duplicates.

features.title: Retrieval function
features.description: Semantic search that returns candidate recipes.
steps: Create recipegen/retrieval.py with retrieve(query, k, cuisine=None) using the SAME embedding model as indexing.
Return recipe id, name, text, metadata and distance.
Treat results as candidates only; do not assume they satisfy user constraints.
Write tests with a tiny temporary Chroma collection.
Manually try 5 queries and record the top results in docs/retrieval_notes.md.
acceptance: Tests pass.
'quick breakfast with potatoes and onions' returns plausible recipes, or the notes say honestly that it does not.

features.title: RAG prompt construction and generation
features.description: Augment the prompt with retrieved recipes and generate the final recipe.
steps: Create recipegen/rag.py with build_rag_prompt(request, retrieved).
Instruct the model to use retrieved recipes as reference only, to respect user constraints over retrieved content, and to say which retrieved ids it used.
Fallback: if retrieval returns nothing useful, use the plain prompt and mark the result as non-RAG.
Extend pipeline.generate_recipe(use_rag=True) and reuse the same response validation.
Write tests/test_rag.py with mocked retrieval and LLM.
acceptance: RAG path and plain path both return validated Recipe objects.
Fallback path is tested.

features.title: RAG controls in the UI
features.description: Let the user switch RAG on or off and see what was retrieved.
steps: Add a 'Use recipe knowledge base (RAG)' toggle to app.py.
Show retrieved recipes in an expander so the user can see the grounding.
Label every result with the mode used (plain / RAG).
acceptance: Toggle changes the pipeline path.
Retrieved sources are visible when RAG is on.
features.verify: streamlit run app.py (manual, both modes with the Phase 6A sample query)

features.title: Evaluation test set
features.description: A fixed set of requests used to compare plain LLM vs RAG.
steps: Create eval/test_cases.json with at least 30 cases: vegetarian, non-veg, eggetarian, tight time, impossible constraints, odd ingredient combinations, South Indian styles, bachelor mode.
Each case lists the request and the checks that apply (diet, time, ingredient usage).
USER: review the cases and approve or edit them before F23 starts.
acceptance: 30+ cases, JSON loads, each case maps to a valid RecipeRequest or is deliberately invalid.
User approval recorded in progress.md.

features.title: Evaluation runner and metrics
features.description: Run every case in both modes and measure.
steps: Create eval/run_eval.py. Run each case with use_rag False and True.

Record: success rate, valid-structured-response rate, ingredient compliance, diet compliance, time compliance, average latency, API error rate, token usage and estimated cost (zero on a free tier, but still record tokens).
Sleep between calls to respect rate limits; handle failures without crashing the run.
Save raw results to eval/results/ as CSV with a timestamp.
acceptance: A full run completes and writes a CSV.
Runner never counts an invalid response as a success.

features.title: LLM vs RAG comparison report
features.description: Honest write-up of what the numbers show.
steps: Create docs/EVAL_REPORT.md with a results table for both modes and the method.
State the conclusion the data supports. If RAG did not help, say so; do not spin it.
List limitations: sample size, keyword-based diet checks, model non-determinism, dataset coverage.
Commit, push, tag v0.2-m2. Append an interviewer-style critique to progress.md.
acceptance: Report contains real numbers from F23.
Limitations section is present and specific.
Tag v0.2-m2 is on GitHub.

features.title: SQLite database module
features.description: Schema and data-access functions for history and favourites.
steps: Create recipegen/db.py with init_db(), save_recipe(), list_recipes(), get_recipe(), set_favourite().
Table columns: id, request_json, recipe_json, created_at, is_favourite, mode (plain/RAG).
Use parameterised queries only, never string-built SQL.
USER: confirm single-user is enough for now. If multi-user is wanted, this feature must be extended with user ids and access control before deployment.
Write tests/test_db.py using a temporary database file.
acceptance: CRUD and favourite toggle tests pass.
Database file is git-ignored.

features.title: Save generated recipes
features.description: Enable the Save button and persist results.
steps: Enable Save in app.py; call db.save_recipe with the request and recipe.
Prevent duplicate saves of the same displayed result on rerun.
Show a confirmation message.
acceptance: A saved recipe appears in the database.
Clicking Save twice does not create two rows for the same result.
features.verify: pytest tests/test_db.py -q ; manual save in the app

features.title: Recipe history view
features.description: List and reopen past recipes.
steps: Add a History page or sidebar section listing recipes newest first.
Clicking an item reopens it in the normal display component.
Handle the empty-history case.
acceptance: Previously saved recipes can be reopened after restarting the app.
features.verify: streamlit run app.py (manual: save, restart, reopen)

features.title: Favourites
features.description: Mark, unmark and filter favourite recipes.
steps: Add a favourite toggle on the recipe display and in history.
Add a 'Favourites only' filter.
acceptance: Favourite state persists across restarts and the filter works.

features.title: Automated test suite hardening
features.description: Close test gaps and add coverage reporting.
steps: Add pytest-cov. Report coverage.
USER: agree a coverage target (suggested 70% on the recipegen package, not including app.py).
Add missing tests for the six example cases listed in Phase 8A.
Mock all network calls so tests run offline.
acceptance: pytest passes with no network.
Coverage meets the agreed target.

features.title: Error handling, logging and abuse limits
features.description: Make failures understandable and the app hard to misuse.
steps: Add standard logging (no secrets, no full user prompts at INFO).
Add a simple per-session cooldown or request cap to protect the API quota.
Review every exception path in pipeline.py and app.py; no raw stack traces reach the user.
Write tests for the cooldown logic.
acceptance: Bad key, no network and rate limit each show a distinct friendly message.
Cooldown tests pass.

features.title: README and documentation
features.description: Recruiter-facing documentation.
steps: README: what it is, screenshots or GIF, architecture diagram (from the workflow summary), setup, env vars, run, test, eval results summary, limitations, disclaimer.
Link docs/EVAL_REPORT.md and docs/DECISIONS.md.
Add a LICENSE after USER chooses one.
acceptance: A stranger can follow the README to run the app (USER confirms on a clean clone).
Eval numbers in README match EVAL_REPORT.md.

features.title: Secrets and repository hygiene check
features.description: Make sure no key ever reaches GitHub.
steps: Search the working tree AND git history for the API key pattern and for .env.
Confirm .env, chroma_db/, the SQLite file and data/raw/ are ignored.
If any key was ever committed: tell the user to rotate it immediately; deleting the commit is not enough.
Pin versions in requirements.txt.
acceptance: No key found in tree or history.
requirements.txt installs cleanly in a fresh venv.
features.verify: git log --all -p -S"GEMINI_API_KEY=" ; git ls-files | findstr /i ".env"  (use grep on Mac/Linux)

features.title: Deploy the app
features.description: Public URL recruiters can open.
steps: Recommended first target: Streamlit Community Cloud (free, simplest). If memory limits break the sentence-transformers + Chroma stack, move to Hugging Face Spaces, which is also recognised in AI/ML circles. Agent must re-check current platform limits before choosing.
USER: decide how the vector index gets there: commit a prebuilt chroma_db (only if the dataset licence allows redistribution) or build it at startup. Record the choice in docs/DECISIONS.md.
USER: add GEMINI_API_KEY in the platform's secrets settings. Never in the repo.
Deploy and record the URL in README.
acceptance: Public URL opens the app.
The key exists only in platform secrets.
features.verify: open the public URL in a private browser window

features.title: Deployment testing
features.description: Run the Phase 9D checklist against the live site.
steps: Site opens; ingredient entry works; a recipe generates; recipe displays correctly.
Invalid input is rejected with a message; a forced API failure shows a friendly message.
Test on a phone browser too.
Fix and redeploy anything that fails; note results in progress.md.
acceptance: Every Phase 9D checklist item passes on the live URL.
features.verify: manual checklist on the live URL

features.title: Portfolio packaging and interview prep
features.description: Turn the finished project into something that gets interviews.
steps: Write 3 resume bullets with real numbers from the eval report.
Record a 2-minute demo GIF or video and link it in the README.
Create docs/INTERVIEW_NOTES.md: 15 likely interview questions (RAG vs plain LLM, embeddings, validation, prompt design, failures found) with answers grounded in THIS project.
Final blunt interviewer-style review of the whole project in progress.md. Tag v1.0.
acceptance: Resume bullets use only numbers that exist in the repo.
Tag v1.0 is on GitHub.
